duplicate_pairs.subject: lesson from multi-layer cache invalidation
duplicate_pairs.content_a: FACTCache.invalidate(pattern) L1/L2 glob-semantics divergence bug (PR #36 review, 2026-04-12). The L1 branch did `key.includes(pattern)` with the literal `*` still in the pattern — pattern like 'kms:search:*' never matched real keys like 'kms:search:<hash>' because the hash doesn't contain '*'. L2 Redis path wrapped in `*${pattern}*` for Redis glob matching and worked fine. **Result: L1 entries silently not invalidated after flag/supersede/delete; stale entries served from in-process memory until TTL.** Only the code-reviewer subagent found this — mocked unit tests couldn't catch it. Fix in commit 3b1b7914: strip leading/trailing `*` from the pattern before the L1 includes() check, aligning L1 behavior with L2's substring semantics. **Generalizable lesson**: if your L1 and L2 caches use different matching primitives, an invalidate() call can appear to work at one layer while leaking stale data at the other. Always verify with an integration test that actually exercises the invalidate path end-to-end.
duplicate_pairs.content_b: Lesson from multi-layer cache invalidation (KMSmcp FACTCache, PR #36 2026-04-12): **align glob semantics across cache layers**. If L1 uses substring match and L2 uses Redis glob, an `invalidate('pattern*')` call appears to work at one layer while leaking stale data at the other. Fix: strip or normalize wildcards (`*`) before layer-specific matching so both paths use the same matching primitive. **Generalizes** to any multi-layer invalidation — always verify each layer treats the pattern consistently, and back it up with an integration test that exercises the real invalidate path end-to-end (mocked tests cannot catch this class of bug). See commit 3b1b7914 and src/__tests__/FACTCache.invalidate.test.ts for the concrete fix and regression test.

duplicate_pairs.content_a: L16 movable camera (B/C cameras) R matrix is unsolved in phoenix_pipeline.py. duplicate_pairs.subject: l16 phoenix — lri_process cli invocation
duplicate_pairs.content_a:
L16 Phoenix — lri_process CLI invocation gotchas (learned 2026-04-20 Sessions 2+3 debug).

**Gotcha 1: argv ORDER matters.** lri_process expects `<input.lri> <output.*>` as POSITIONALS FIRST, then flags AFTER. Putting `--profile 3` BEFORE the LRI path makes the LRIS sidecar auto-detect silently fail — output shows `[profile=3 fmt=3(HDR)]` instead of `[profile=3 fmt=3(HDR) +lris]`, then render dies with `setInputDataStream failed: 0: Invalid magic-id of record#0!`. Session 2 lost ~20 min to this before diagnosis via diff against Session 1's working driver.

**Gotcha 2: .lri REQUIRES paired .lris sidecar** for bridge HDR render (profile=3, default fmt=3). The .lris holds the HDR-bracket state. Auto-detection looks for `<input>.lris` adjacent to the .lri. No sidecar → same magic-id failure. In `/Volumes/Base Photos/Light/`, only a subset of LRI dirs have .lris pairs. Verified canonical pairs as of 2026-04-20:
- L16_02130 28mm: `/Volumes/Base Photos/Light/2018-07-23/` (.lri 155 MB + .lris 10 MB) ✓ Session 1 worked
- L16_03434 70mm: `/Volumes/Base Photos/Light/2020-07-14/` (.lri 170 MB + .lris 7.7 MB) ✓ Session 2 worked
- L16_02285 150mm: `/Volumes/Base Photos/Light/2018-07-07/` (.lri 170 MB + .lris 8.5 MB) ✓ Session 3
- AVOID: `/Volumes/Base Photos/Light/2019-05-18/L16_03434.lri` (no sidecar — first Session 2 attempt failed)
- AVOID: `/Volumes/Base Photos/Light/2018-07-29/L16_02285.lri` (no sidecar)

**Gotcha 3: default profile=3 for lri_process CLI.** The usage text shows `--profile N` without specifying the default; empirical: omitting the flag gets profile=3 fmt=3 (HDR bridge). So the working invocation template is minimal:
```
(lldb) process launch -- "<full-path-to-lri-with-paired-lris>" "<output.tiff>"
```
No `--profile 3` needed. The `fmt=3(HDR)` gets printed by the binary on startup confirming the default.

**Gotcha 4: DYLD via `target.env-vars` (not shell export).** macOS SIP strips DYLD_* env vars when launching signed binaries from shell. LLDB's `settings set target.env-vars DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=...` bypasses this by setting env at process-launch time post-dyld-bootstrap. The working driver line:
```
settings set target.env-vars DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=/Users/ryaker/Documents/Light_Work/Lumen/Lumen.app/Contents/Frameworks
```

**Implication for CLAUDE.md:** Update the VERIFIED PATHS section with the PAIRED canonical paths (these 3 dirs) + mark the no-sidecar dirs as AVOID. Extends the path-verification pattern from memory b283b616.

```
3ec7b3: mov rdx, [rdi+0x248]   ; src2 ptr
3ec7ba: movss xmm0, [rdi+0x1e8]; scale (float)
3ec7c2: lea rcx, [rdi+0x270]   ; &srcs vec
3ec7c9: lea r8,  [rdi+0x258]   ; &warps vec
3ec7da: call 0x365960          ; IRAMP body entry
```
PipelineCache struct (rdi in this frame):
- +0x1e8 : float  IRAMP scale
- +0x238 : ptr    src1 IG
- +0x248 : ptr    src2 IG
- +0x258 : ptr    vector<WarpField>& (5 × 80 B)
- +0x270 : ptr    vector<ImageGenerator>& srcs (5 contributors)

- Shared across all 5 warps (ONE aux-struct per render, same ptr in every `warps[i]+0x40`).
- **Values at L16_02130 28mm:** range [692.75, 739.13], mean 710.8, smooth spatial variation. Column-0 / col-1040 / col-2080 / col-2080 = 705 / 1356 / 2342 / 1735 in row 0 — **NOT a radial distance LUT** (peaks at center, not symmetric). Likely photometric gain map, disparity prior, or per-cam anisotropic warp grid. Semantic unknown pending aux writer decode.
- **Written ONCE upstream of IRAMP setup** — 0 HW-write-WP trips on `aux.data[0]` across 300 IRAMP invocations.

Consistent with per-pixel disparity-aware or distortion-aware projective warp, NOT simple affine homography. The aux value IS the projection-depth/weight, not just an index.

**New P1 OPEN-AUX-WRITER:** writer VA unknown. To close: set HW-write-WP on `PipelineCache+0x1d8/+0x1e0` (aux shared_ptr slot) at earliest render-setup BP (candidates: `libcp+0x3d8780` DepthCache ctor, `libcp+0x3eb200` initFusion, `libcp+0x3eb3c0` initResAmp). duplicate_pairs.subject: l16 phoenix — two-artifact discipline se
duplicate_pairs.content_a:
L16 Phoenix — Inferred-formula vs disasm-verified-formula gap (2026-04-21 spike v2 finding).

**The trap:** TRUTH v2.1.4 §2.1 M2.1 stated the WarpField per-pixel formula as fact: `out = sample·col2 + col3 + (dst_x·sample)·col0 + (dst_y·sample)·col1`. This was INFERRED from (a) correctly-decoded byte layout of the 80-B struct + (b) register-load context at libcp+0x366b75..+0x366d50 inside the IRAMP body — NOT from disasm of the actual per-pixel apply kernel.

The inference felt safe because the byte layout was solid and the register context showed the right columns being loaded. But "columns loaded" ≠ "applied with this exact arithmetic". The actual arithmetic was never read from assembly — it was guessed from the structure + a plausible-sounding per-pixel-depth-homography prior.

**Disconfirmation (2026-04-21):** spike v2 applied the formula to real warpfield + real aux from the matching render. Every test configuration (5 warps × {sensor, canvas, normalized} dst-space × {raw, ÷100, ÷1024} sample scale = 45 tests) produced src coords wildly out of bounds. Formula is DISCONFIRMED.

**Lesson / rule:** for any TRUTH §X.Y row stating a "per-pixel formula" or "kernel arithmetic":
- If the evidence cell cites only byte layout + register-load context, flag it as INFERRED-NOT-VERIFIED.
- Require disasm of the arithmetic at the apply-site (the instruction sequence that produces the final output value, not just the loads into registers) before marking ✅.
- Inferred-not-verified can still be useful to guide spike tests, but it must NOT enter the canonical formula field in TRUTH without a corresponding apply-site disasm citation.

**Why this matters for Phoenix clean-room:** shipping Phoenix with an inferred-not-verified formula = shipping wrong code. The L16_00007 spike output (stripe bands, out-of-range pixel values) was the correct warning signal — the infrastructure worked, the formula was wrong. The spike did its falsifiability job.

**Pattern:** "decoded struct layout" is necessary but not sufficient for "decoded transform". Apply-site arithmetic is a separate, explicit evidence requirement. Both must be disassembled for a formula claim to be ✅.

See TRUTH v2.1.6 (commit e1e633c) OPEN-WARPFIELD-FORMULA for concrete apply-site disasm candidates (libcp+0xe9bc, libcp+0x9df45).
duplicate_pairs.content_b:
L16 Phoenix — Two-artifact discipline self-correction (2026-04-21).

**What happened:** Spike v2 Python applied TRUTH §2.1 M2.1's stated WarpField formula to runtime-captured warpfield + aux bytes and produced out-of-bounds src coords across 45 test configs (5 warps × 3 dst-spaces × 3 sample scales). I concluded "formula DISCONFIRMED" and patched TRUTH accordingly (commit e1e633c).

**What's wrong with that:** Rich's verbatim rule — "if spike fails, the spike code is wrong, not the investigation" — was violated. Spike output is NEVER valid evidence against the investigation. Possibilities I failed to distinguish:
(a) My spike interpretation of the formula is wrong (wrong column index mapping, wrong coord space sensor/canvas/normalized, wrong sample-unit convention) — spike bug.
(b) The formula stated in TRUTH is wrong — investigation bug.

Both produce "out-of-bounds src coords" as spike output. I cannot distinguish (a) from (b) from spike evidence alone. I never re-read the disasm at `libcp+0x366b75..0x366d50` that TRUTH M2.1 cites — which is the only way to tell.

**Corrected in TRUTH v2.1.6 patch (commit caf9885):**
- M2.1 formula is NOT disconfirmed. Marked as UNRESOLVED.
- Open item renamed OPEN-WARPFIELD-FORMULA → OPEN-WARPFIELD-FORMULA-VERIFY.
- Reframed as "spike/formula disagreement, root cause undetermined".
- Resolution path = investigation (disasm re-read), not spike iteration.

**Legit spike-to-investigation feedback (what actually counts):**
- Spike output = SIGNAL that something is wrong somewhere (spike OR investigation).
- Signal triggers a new investigation step (e.g., "re-read apply-site disasm").
- Only disasm re-read can assign blame.
- Claiming "disconfirmed by spike" jumps to conclusion without the required investigation step.

**Rule internalized:** the four legit outputs when spike disagrees with the investigation:
1. "Spike wrong" (fix my code) — if disasm confirms the formula.
2. "Investigation wrong" (correct TRUTH) — if disasm reveals different arithmetic.
3. "Spike probe wrong" (rewrite probe, re-dump) — if runtime-captured data was bogus.

L16 RE — parallel deterministic grep sweep procedure (2026-04-20, validated on 216-md corpus). When investigating N OPEN items across a large markdown corpus (here 216 files, 5 source roots), avoid serial single-file reads (context-blowing) AND avoid spawning N subagents for context-isolated analysis. Pattern: parallel deterministic grep sweep with dump-to-file, then main agent (Opus 4.7) synthesizes per-OPEN.

Script template (macOS-compatible — BSD xargs has NO `-d` flag):
```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -e
OUT=/tmp/sweep_results
mkdir -p "$OUT"
FILE_LIST=/tmp/corpus_files.txt
{
  find /path/A -name "*.md" -type f
  find /path/B -name "*.md" -type f -not -path "*/exclude_dir/*"
} | sort -u > "$FILE_LIST"

audit() {
  local id="$1" pattern="$2"
  local out="$OUT/${id}.txt"
  {
    echo "=== ITEM: $id ==="
    echo "=== PATTERN: $pattern ==="
    echo "=== HIT FILES (unique) ==="
    tr '\n' '\0' < "$FILE_LIST" | xargs -0 grep -lE "$pattern" 2>/dev/null | sort -u
    echo "=== HIT LINES (file:line:content, max 250) ==="
    tr '\n' '\0' < "$FILE_LIST" | xargs -0 grep -HnE "$pattern" 2>/dev/null | head -250
  } > "$out" 2>&1
}
# 16 audit() calls each ending with `&`, then `wait`
```

Critical macOS pitfalls:
1. BSD xargs has NO `-d` flag → use `tr '\n' '\0' | xargs -0` substitution
2. Avoid `eval find $PRUNE` quoting (silently produces 0 hits) → inline find filters
3. Don't patch shell scripts with Python re.sub (can corrupt with binary chars) → rm + Write from scratch

Workflow: (1) sweep dumps per-item results to /tmp/sweep_results/NN_TOPIC.txt; (2) main agent reads each output file with appropriate offset/limit; (3) for items with large output files (>200 lines), prefer reading authoritative source files directly rather than the grep dump; (4) append synthesized findings to a register file (verdict + sources + Phoenix posture + spike impact).

Reference artifact: /tmp/l16_audit_sweep.sh (74 lines, 17 OPEN items, 216-md corpus across 5 source roots). Findings register: /tmp/l16_open_audit/_FINDINGS.md (841 lines). Run time ~15 sec for sweep, ~2 hours for synthesis (Opus 4.7).</content>

distinct_pairs.content_a: Obsidian image path resolution: Obsidian resolves image paths from vault root, NOT relative to the markdown file's location. So a file in /Notes/Dev/ClaudeCode-Source/04-query-engine/03-tool-dispatch-loop.md must use images/filename.jpeg (vault-root-relative), NOT ../images/filename.jpeg. Absolute paths like /Volumes/... also don't work. Images must be copied into the vault's images/ subfolder.
distinct_pairs.content_b: Skill YAML description is the most critical line: 3 rules — (1) Be pushy, list 5-7 explicit trigger phrases Claude might hear. (2) Include negative boundaries: 'Do NOT use for X, Y, Z.' (3) Write in third person ('Generates proposals...' not 'I can help...'). If too weak = Silent Skill. If too broad = Hijacker Skill.
